answer: An agent economy deploys game-theoretic multi-agent auditing paired with topological cut verifications across transaction graphs. Agents stake capital to audit peer clusters; any detected identity split triggers stake slashing. By enforcing high minimum-cut capacities, isolating a fake cluster requires spanning an expanding canyon of collateral rather than shifting a single dune of identity. Anchoring nodes with a rigid, ferrous stake lockup forces an attacker to incur superlinear costs scaling with network partition depth.
